title: Fppf cohomology vanishes for modules zero on flat locally finitely presented tests
statement: Fix universes and small presentations of sites as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal C_S=(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ be its big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] with structure sheaf $\mathcal O(v:V\to S)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. Let $P$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose $P(V)=0$ for every object $v:V\to S$ which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then, for every such $v$ and every integer $q\geq0$, $$R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(V,-)(P)=0.$$ Here $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(V,-)$ is evaluation at $v$ with values in abelian groups, and its right derived functors are computed by injective resolutions in the category of structure-module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. In particular all these groups vanish at $\operatorname{id}_S$. No affineness or quasi-coherence assumption on $S,V,P$ is imposed, and nothing is assumed about $P(W)$ for maps $W\to S$ outside the specified class.

source.place: Tag 0755 (lemma-cohomology-parasitic), part (1), tau = fppf; the hypothesis is the explicit sectionwise form of being parasitic for the fppf topology in Tag 06ZL (definition-parasitic). Cohomology of modules agrees with underlying abelian cohomology by sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree).

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B$ consist of the objects $v:V\to S$ that are flat and locally of finite presentation, and let $\mathrm{Cov}$ consist of all fppf coverings of objects of $\mathcal B$. By the definition of the big fppf site each covering arrow $V_i\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Composition preserves both properties by [lem-pc-flat-compose] and [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition], so $V_i\to S$ belongs to $\mathcal B$. For a tuple $(i_0,\ldots,i_p)$ define $W_0=V_{i_0}$ and $W_r=W_{r-1}\times_V V_{i_r}$ for $1\le r\le p$. The projection $W_r\to W_{r-1}$ is a base change of $V_{i_r}\to V$, hence is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and locally of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Induction on $r$, starting with the preceding assertion for $W_0$, and the same composition results show $W_r\to S\in\mathcal B$. Thus all nonempty iterated fibre products required in the Cech criterion lie in $\mathcal B$. Every covering of an object in $\mathcal B$ already belongs to $\mathrm{Cov}$, so the cofinality requirement is satisfied by the covering itself and its identity refinement. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness assertion is used.

source.place: Tag 0755, label lemma-cohomology-parasitic, proof for the fppf topology; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03F9, label lemma-cech-vanish-collection

proof.text: Let $F=P_{ab}$ be the underlying abelian sheaf. For every covering $\mathcal U=\{V_i\to V\}$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$ and $p\ge0$, the preceding step places every $W_{i_0\ldots i_p}$ in $\mathcal B$, so the hypothesis gives $F(W_{i_0\ldots i_p})=0$. By [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] the degree-$p$ term is $\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)}F(W_{i_0\ldots i_p})=0$. Therefore every differential has zero source and target, and $\check H^p(\mathcal U,F)=\ker(0\to0)/\operatorname{im}(0\to0)=0$. This also handles an empty index set: the empty product in abelian groups is the zero group.

source.place: Tag 0755, label lemma-cohomology-parasitic, proof for the fppf topology; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03F9, label lemma-cech-vanish-collection

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] to $\mathcal C_S$, $\mathcal B$, $\mathrm{Cov}$ and $F$: closure of covering objects and intersections, cofinality, and positive Cech vanishing were verified in steps 1 and 2. It follows that $H^q(V,F)=0$ for every $V\to S$ in $\mathcal B$ and $q>0$. In the small presentation fixed in the statement, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] applies to the actual structure ring sheaf $\mathcal O$, and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] gives enough injectives in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] applies at every object $V$ and gives $R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(V,-)(P)\cong H^q(V,F)=0$ for $q>0$. This is comparison for a variable structure sheaf, not for constant coefficients; it does not assume that forgetting scalars preserves injectivity.

source.place: Tag 03F9, label lemma-cech-vanish-collection; Tag 03FD, label lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, equality over an object; injectives.tex Tags 079Q and 079H for module injective resolutions

proof.text: In degree zero the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] is the identity of $P(V)$, so $R^0\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(V,-)(P)=P(V)=0$ by hypothesis. Finally $\operatorname{id}_S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation: its stalk maps are identity maps, a ring is flat over itself (tensoring with it is the identity), and on an affine chart its identity algebra has a presentation with no variables and no relations. These are exactly the flatness and local finite-presentation definitions. Hence $\operatorname{id}_S\in\mathcal B$, giving the stated particular case, including when $S$ is empty.
